name: kimi-ahk-design-str
goal:
You are the campaign ARCHITECT for module 1 of the plan you wrote (PLAN.md): str.ahk, the building block. A crew member (a cheap model) will write str.ahk from YOUR contract and be judged by YOUR hidden tests, which it never sees. A second member writes its own tests from the contract alone. Design it so a careful small model passes on the first try and a careless one cannot pass by accident.

THE PA'S ANSWERS TO YOUR OPEN QUESTIONS:
1. A module_author_ahk post now exists (Hoss, Nemotron, Qwen - unproven on AHK). Your team for str.ahk stands: author Hoss, tester Qwen.
2. A module MAY #Include another crew module it depends on (the campaign's depends list); keep str.ahk self-contained - it depends on nothing.
3. Default/Coalesce: the empty string is the ONLY empty value; 0, "0" and false are values. Write that as a numbered rule with examples.
4. (csv, later) lenient, like the stock library.
5. StrSplit is AutoHotkey v1.1 (since 1.1.13) and may be used.
6. Campaign 2 order: the pure repeated-press timer state comes next, then list helpers, then escaping.

FIXED RULES OF THE JUDGE: read crew/contracts/ahk_scan.md (what the static scanner refuses: banned words, '%', hotkeys, labels, loose code, #Include outside the whitelist) and ahk_api.md (how the API/stub checks read functions). Tests are AutoHotkey v1.1 files that begin with exactly `#Include tap.ahk` then `#Include str.ahk`, use only Is(got, want, name) (compares with ==, so case-sensitive), Ok(condition, name) and end with Done(); read crew/ahk/tap.ahk. No labels, hotkeys, '%' or outside-world commands in tests either. They run inside a disposable Windows Sandbox; you cannot run them - the PA will, against your reference implementation, before any crew member sees the contract. So be exact: every expected value must be what real AutoHotkey v1.1 returns.

CONTRACT STRUCTURE: copy the structure of the house contracts in crew/contracts (e.g. st_mission.md): purpose, a Public API block with every function signature and return value, numbered rules, worked examples, and the edge cases stated outright (empty input, non-ASCII letters in Lower/Upper/Title - say what StringLower/StringUpper do with them, numbers passed where text is expected, Title on already-mixed case and on words with apostrophes, Coalesce with zero arguments and with only empty strings, input variables left unchanged). Do not write an 'Allowed imports' line; write 'Allowed: AutoHotkey v1.1 built-in functions and commands that only compute a value (StringLower, StringUpper, StrLen, SubStr, InStr, StrSplit, RegExReplace...). Nothing that touches windows, keys, clipboard, files, registry or time.'

STAGE EXACTLY THESE FILES with stage_file:
1. str.md - the contract.
2. str.ahk - your reference implementation (it must pass the scanner rules above: every line inside a function, no '%').
3. test_str.ahk - the hidden tests: at least 30 Is/Ok checks, each check's name naming the contract rule it covers (e.g. "rule 4: Default keeps \"0\""); exact expected values, never just Ok(value != "").
4. campaign.json - in this shape: {"name": "ahk-str", "senior": "Claude", "senior_fallback": "Kimi", "max_attempts": 3, "max_escalations": 0, "max_requests": 40, "workspace_subdir": "ahk_lib", "goal": "...", "teams": {"Strings": {"author": "Hoss", "tester": "Qwen"}}, "tasks": [{"id": "str", "team": "Strings", "module": "str.ahk", "contract": "C:/Users/user/ATLAS-api-harness/crew/contracts/ahk_str.md", "hidden_tests": ["C:/Users/user/ATLAS-api-harness/crew/hidden_tests/test_str.ahk"], "api": [every public function name], "depends": [], "min_tests": 12, "instructions": "...the two quirks most likely to trip the author...", "test_instructions": "..."}]}.

Final answer: the API in one paragraph, the three checks in test_str.ahk you are least sure real AutoHotkey agrees with (the PA will look at those first in the sandbox run), and anything in the contract you had to decide without a source.
